stem: Why is the adolescent stage described as a potential 'major loss on health investment'?

options.text: Health gains made in childhood through vaccinations and nutrition are often not maintained.
Adolescents require more expensive medical technology than children or adults.
Health professionals usually ignore adolescents until they become adults.
The transition to adult care is so complex that most data is lost.

explanation: The speaker notes that the success of childhood health interventions can be lost if health trajectories are not managed during adolescence.
rationale: Focus on what happens to the benefits of early childhood interventions during this transition period.

optionExplanations.A: The speaker notes that the success of childhood health interventions can be lost if health trajectories are not managed during adolescence.
optionExplanations.B: The 'loss' refers to the sustainability of health outcomes rather than the specific cost of medical equipment.
optionExplanations.C: While the speaker mentions some professionals assume they will 'grow out of it,' the investment loss is specifically linked to the erosion of childhood health gains.
optionExplanations.D: Data management is a separate issue; the primary concern is the physical and mental health trajectory set during this time.

source.hint: Focus on what happens to the benefits of early childhood interventions during this transition period.
